To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we identified 21 differentially expressed proteins by proteomic analysis in HER-2-positive breast cancer.
we have identified novel modulating proteins in HER-2 positive breast cancers.
the differential proteome analysis of microdissected breast tumours revealed 21 proteins that are differentially expressed in HER-2-positive tumours.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of proteins associated with HER- 2/neu over-expression, and provides a basis for further investigation of the molecular mechanism of HER-2/ neu signalling in cancer.
the identification of proteins differentially expressed in HER-2-positive breast tumours, which may be useful in the development of novel therapeutic targets.
the proteomic characterization of breast cancer and provides evidence for the association of hnRNP H1, GRP78 and RKIP expression with HER-2 status.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

HER-2/neuligand binding induces hnRNP Hl expression, which may in turn regulate HER-2/neutarget gene expression, and that HER-2/ neu-ligand binding inhibits GRP78 andRKIP expression, which may inhibit HER-2/neusignalling.
hnRNP H, GRP78/Bip and RKIP are novel HER-2/neumodulated proteins, which are associated with tumour progression in breast cancer.
hnRNP H, GRP78 and Raf-1 inhibitor are novel modulators of HER-2-driven breast cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the differential expression of hnRNP-H1, GRP78 and/or RKIP could be used as prognostic markers and therapeutic targets for HER-2/neumodulated breast cancer.
hnRNP H, RKIP and Grp78/Bip may serve as novel biomarkers and potential therapeutic targets for the management of breast cancer.
hnRNP H and RKIP are potential prognostic markers and therapeutic targets of HER-2-positive breast cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
hnRNP H, GRP78 and Raf-1 inhibitor protein are differentially expressed and are likely to be implicated in HER-2-driven tumourigenic processes.
we identified three proteins, hnRNP H, GRP78 and Raf-1, that have not been previously linked to HER- 2/neu signalling.
the differential expression of hnRNP, GRP78 and Raf-1 is strongly associated with the HER-2/Neu status.
